item.title: On physical implementability of reinforcement-learning-driven reasoning
item.description: arXiv:2610.14131v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the machine learning community, the reinforcement-learning-driven reasoning process has been intensively studied since around 2025. In this article, we present a negative result on the hardware implementation of this reinforcement-learning-driven reasoning process in a physical neural network model in the presence of a reward external potential energy for a given reward. In this hardware implementation, the existence of a chain of thought in dynamics contradicts the Lyapunov stability of the system.
item.dc:creator: Eiji Konishi

item.title: Weyl's theorem and the theoretical origin of Boson peak in two-dimensional scalar spring network
item.description: arXiv:2610.15318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The origin of the anomalous low-frequency vibrational density of states (VDOS) universally observed in amorphous solids has been debated for decades. In this work, we model amorphous solids as a zero-temperature scalar spring network, the simplest model that captures both the amorphous structure and the features of the anomalous VDOS. Using this scalar network, we mathematically demonstrate that disorder can lead to a shift of the VDOS toward low frequencies, thereby accumulating the anomalous part there. Disorder is defined through the topological connectivity of the network. The validity and universality of the theoretical framework are general and valuable for real-world scenarios because it rests only on Weyl's theorem for Hermitian matrices and is free of perturbation and phenomenological assumptions. This work strips away complex factors and reveals, at the level of mathematical principles, a profound and clean mechanism for the origin of the anomalous VDOS in amorphous solids.
item.dc:creator: Cunyuan Jiang

item.title: Eigenstate transitions and critical transport in 3D Aubry-Andr\'e model
item.description: arXiv:2610.15842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We numerically study spectral and wave-function properties, as well as time evolution, in finite-size commensurate approximations of the 3D Aubry-Andr\'e model. We explicitly show, through scaling analysis, the existence of two critical points. One of the critical points is a localization-delocalization transition in real-space, similar to the critical point in the 3D Anderson model. The other is a localization-delocalization transition in a dual momentum space, which does not have any analog in the 3D Anderson model. We estimate their values from spectral measures, such as the gap ratio and the spectral form factor, as well as from wave-function measures, such as the inverse participation ratio and the participation entropy. Additionally, we demonstrate that both critical points exhibit hallmarks of critical points between quantum ergodicity and localization. First, the eigenstates and the eigenspectrum at the critical point fulfill the mutual universal relation between the eigenspectrum compressibility $\chi$ and the eigenstate fractal dimension $d^{(1)}$ [S. Jiricek et al., Proc. Nat. Acad. Sci. 123, e2518027123 (2026)]. Second, the dynamics of the wave packet at the critical point is governed by the critical dynamical exponent $z$, characterized by the spectral fractal dimension and the dimensionality of the lattice [M. Hopjan and L. Vidmar, Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 060401 (2025)]. Thus, similarly to the 3D Anderson model, the critical dynamical exponent is sub-diffusive with the value of $z=3$.
item.dc:creator: Pragna Das, Lev Vidmar, Miroslav Hopjan

item.title: Quantum Localization in Geometric Complex Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.15874v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum localization, the phenomenon by which wave diffusion is halted, here understood as the superposition of propagating waves, can have many different origins, such as onsite random potentials in Anderson localization. However, some systems exhibit complex geometries and could potentially reproduce similar results without external potentials. In this work, we study how localization of single particle states is affected by the underlying topology of a simple but highly predictive complex network model: the geometric soft configuration model $\mathbb S^1$. By tuning the model's temperature and heterogeneity parameters, we are able to generate different structural patterns and focus on the transition from a small-world to a non-small-world regime. Our study suggests that small-world networks tend to have extended states, which spread the whole system's size, in contrast to non-small-world networks which tend to localize, showing how complex connectivity can play the role assigned to random energetic disorder.
item.dc:creator: Jan Lewenstein-Sanpera, Tobias Grass, M. \`Angeles Serrano, Bruno Juli\'a-D\'iaz

item.title: Orbital cancellation and reentrant localization in a quasiperiodic trimer ladder
item.description: arXiv:2610.16197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Uniform orbital detuning can restore spatial extent even as quasiperiodic modulation strengthens. In a trimer ladder with fixed hoppings and orbital modulation signs, increasing detuning and modulation amplitude together drives successive avoided crossings that redistribute orbital weights, suppressing the projected onsite potential in both lower molecular bands while leaving the third strongly modulated. Complete-band participation scaling supports two reentrant high-participation windows, with wave-packet propagation corroborating spatial recovery at representative controls over the studied sizes and times. These diagonal cancellations leave residual interband modulation, which generates a self-energy whose magnitude depends on the molecular level separation. Gaussian quadrature improves convergence of closed-walk determinant estimates used to cross-check energy-resolved attenuation. Comparing the coupled and decoupled ladders under the same finite-size participation criterion shows that restoring the full off-diagonal modulation narrows both sampled windows, with a larger absolute contraction of the second.
item.dc:creator: Xin Wang, Pei-Jie Chang, Quanfeng Lu, Muxi Zheng, Dong Ruan, Gui-Lu long

item.title: Full Lyapunov Spectra of Random Neural Networks, Part I: Finite-Time and Asymptotic Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.14922v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a dynamical mean-field framework for the full finite-time and stationary asymptotic Lyapunov spectra of random recurrent neural networks. At finite observation time, an exact log-determinant representation of tangent-propagator singular values leads to a closed-contour matrix Dyson equation for the smoothed spectral tail. In the stationary setting, a cocycle representation yields an operator equation for the asymptotic cumulative spectrum. Both formulations retain complete local gain histories and the repeated action of quenched connectivity. Direct singular-value calculations and network QR spectra support the predictions in the regimes examined, with sampling uncertainty and numerical cutoffs assessed separately. The stationary equation also recovers the known maximal exponent, and controlled gain-history replay illustrates how temporal correlations redistribute instability. This work was carried out in collaboration with ChatGPT 5.6 Sol. Toward the end of preparation we became aware of David G. Clark's contemporaneous work, \emph{Lyapunov spectrum of random neural networks}[arXiv:2610.12426], which reports overlapping mean-field results for the full Lyapunov spectrum using a cavity approach.
item.dc:creator: Haoyu Albert Wang, Wei P. Dai

item.title: The R\'enyi area law conjecture is false below $\alpha=1$ in high dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.15199v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Area laws express the expectation that entanglement in gapped quantum ground states scales with a boundary rather than a volume. In one dimension this holds for every R\'enyi entropy, and the R\'enyi area-law conjecture asserts the same in higher dimensions for each fixed $0<\alpha<1$. Here we disprove this conjecture in every spatial dimension two and higher. We construct finite-range Hamiltonians with fixed local dimension, bounded interaction strength, unique ground states and a uniform spectral gap, whose ground states exhibit volume-law R\'enyi entanglement while obeying a von Neumann area law and remaining connected to product states through uniformly gapped local paths. The mechanism is error-space complexity: locally identifiable components of arbitrarily small weight can encode states with high entanglement complexity. We also establish the worst-case rank-error trade-off for approximate ground-state projectors, a key tool in one-dimensional area-law proofs. At fixed gap, the optimal Schmidt rank at projection error $\epsilon$ across a planar cut of cross-section $A$ scales as $\exp[\tilde{\Theta}((A\log\epsilon^{-1})^{2/3})]$ when $\log\epsilon^{-1}\gtrsim A$. Thus $\alpha=1$ is the sharp threshold for a universal R\'enyi area law within this adiabatically connected class.
item.dc:creator: Tomotaka Kuwahara

item.title: Generalized Constraint-Controlled Rheological Model: Two Constitutive Pathways under Sinusoidal Periodic Shear Deformation
item.description: arXiv:2610.15538v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We formulate the Generalized Constraint-Controlled Rheological Model (GCCRM) for entangled linear and long-arm-branched polymer melts under sinusoidal periodic shear deformation (SPSD), spanning the linear and strongly nonlinear regimes. Molecular architecture, conformation, chain stretch, flow-active constraints, convective constraint release, dynamic tube dilation, and activated arm retraction define a common upstream molecular state. This state feeds two time-domain constitutive pathways (a configurational stress and a dissipative internal-variable stress) which are recombined before Fourier analysis. For branched polymers, the architecture is described by an entire backbone of molecular weight $M_{bb}$ and $N_a$ long arms of molecular weight $M_a$, with a compliance-weighted representative-constitutive-cell partition. The linear limit is normalized so that the configurational moduli sum to the entanglement modulus, while dynamic tube dilation and stretch drive distinct contributions to dissipative activation. Under reduced closures, GCCRM generates a smooth nonlinear elastic response with an onset of nonlinearity, an approximately logarithmic growth regime, an architecture-dependent maximum, and distinct high-deformation asymptotes. Fourier harmonics, ELR, VLR, and Lissajous curves are treated as post-processing observables of the total stress. The framework establishes a consistent constitutive architecture whose quantitative validation requires one parameter set per material across SPSD and, prospectively, transient shear histories.
item.dc:creator: Dario Nichetti, Alessio Zaccone

item.title: Ergodicity breaking transition beyond qubits
item.description: arXiv:2610.15546v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The local Hilbert space dimension is a fundamental parameter in quantum many-body systems, but its role in controlling the ergodicity-breaking transition remains less explored. We systematically study this question by introducing toy models of qudits in zero dimensions that exhibit an ergodicity-breaking transition. Using the hybridization condition, we analytically obtain the dependence of the critical value of the interactions on the local Hilbert space dimension. Numerical studies of spectral correlation measures show agreement with the theoretical predictions, hence confirming the existence of the ergodicity-breaking transition in these models. We further introduce a distinct higher spin version of the model and numerically obtain the same critical behavior, demonstrating that the observed critical point is independent of the microscopic structure of interactions considered.
item.dc:creator: Tanay Pathak, Abhik Kumar Saha

item.title: Fisher information and the geometry of memorization in neural networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.16161v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A fruitful approach towards understanding generalization in machine learning involves characterizing how models separate generalizable structure from idiosyncratic or even corrupted features of training data. Fisher information has emerged as a diagnostic tool for this separation, leveraging loss geometry to distinguish generalization from memorization. Here we investigate this connection in vision models trained on CIFAR-10 with controlled noise that can be learned only through memorization. We show that projecting model weights onto the top Fisher eigenvectors decouples general task performance from noisy sample memorization, and we investigate how this decoupling presents differentially across layers. We show that the same phenomena are present in small transformers trained to solve a synthetic in-context learning task, and are reproduced in closed form in a simple, analytically solvable linear model. Our results reveal that Fisher information captures aspects of the geometric structure underlying how neural networks allocate capacity between generalization and memorization.
item.dc:creator: Daniel T. Bernstein, Chase Goddard, Luca Di Carlo, Vudtiwat Ngampruetikorn, David J. Schwab

item.title: Probe Signatures of Quantum Chaos with Quantum Sensing
item.description: arXiv:2610.16181v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The spectral form factor (SFF), which is the Fourier transform of the two-point spectral correlation, is a fundamental diagnostics of quantum chaos. Nevertheless, its experimental detection in quantum many-body systems was less unexplored until recently. Here, we establish a relationship between the SFF with the quantum Fisher information (QFI) by means of quantum sensing protocols. Furthermore, when the eigenvalues and eigenstates of the disordered Hamiltonian are statistically independent, we prove that QFI is typical both in short and long timescales while numerics suggest that it is also typical at intermediate timescales, which ensures self-averaging of QFI. The self-averaging property renders the experimental measurement of QFI with our protocol less noisy in contrast with the direct measurement of SFF which is known to be non-self-averaging. Our results reveal an intriguing connection between quantum noise and the signatures of quantum chaos.
item.dc:creator: Isa\'ias Vallejo-Fabila, Jing Yang

item.title: Thermal softening of the yield stress in glasses with different stability
item.description: arXiv:2610.16424v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The yielding of amorphous solids has been extensively studied in the athermal limit, but the influence of thermal fluctuations is much less understood, in particular for glasses of different stability. Using molecular dynamics simulations of a model glass where the swap Monte Carlo algorithm can be employed, we study the yield stress at finite temperature and shear rate, both in steady flow and at shear start-up, over a broad range of glass stability. Thermal fluctuations soften both the dynamic yield stress in steady state and the start-up yield stress. In all cases, the temperature dependence is compatible with the $T^{2/3}$ law expected for thermally activated yielding near a saddle-node instability, with no systematic dependence of the exponent on stability or shear rate. Extrapolations to zero temperature recover the athermal yield stresses. The amplitude of the softening at start-up, by contrast, depends strongly on stability: highly stable glasses are much less sensitive to temperature than poorly annealed ones. A description of yielding at finite temperature must therefore account explicitly for the stability of the glass.
item.dc:creator: Tianze Wan, Ludovic Berthier

item.title: Activity-Induced Structural and Dynamical Heterogeneity in Colloidal Gels
item.description: arXiv:2610.16553v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Active gels are intrinsically non-equilibrium materials whose structural and dynamical heterogeneity emerges from the interplay of attractive interactions, thermal fluctuations, and self-propulsion. We investigate a model active gel, simulated using large-scale Brownian dynamics simulations, to explore the effects of temperature $T$, active force strength $f_0$, persistence timescale $\tau_p$, and active particle concentration $\rho_a$. We characterize the structure of the evolving gel network through morphological analysis, while dynamical changes are quantified by the relaxation timescale and dynamical heterogeneity (DH). We show that an optimal choice of activity parameters yields a percolating gel network with faster gelation and larger voids and clusters, enhancing mechanical stability. Conversely, the structural relaxation timescale and DH decrease with increasing activity, indicating enhanced particle rearrangements and reduced spatial correlations of mobile and immobile regions. An effective temperature ($T_\text{eff}$) framework for colloidal gels maps structural quantities and relaxation timescales in an active gel onto those of a passive gel. More interestingly, the growth of DH with increasing swim force can also be described by the same effective-temperature framework, in stark contrast to observations in active glasses. Our findings show that, in colloidal gels, temperature and active force compete, giving rise to similar structural ordering and, consequently, similar DH at the same $T_\text{eff}$. These findings highlight the crucial role of structural ordering in governing DH in active colloidal gels, as compared to active glasses.
item.dc:creator: Santu Nath, Sudipta Mandal, Smarajit Karmakar

item.title: Whither quantum advantage? New classical lower bounds for Max-Cut on large-girth 3-regular graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.17236v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Every 3-regular graph of girth at least $g$ has a cut containing at least a fraction $M_g$ of its edges, and the best rigorous bounds at large girth are $0.912\le \lim_{g\to\infty}M_g \le 0.92386$. Lower bounds on $M_g$ follow from the performance of local algorithms: on a graph of girth $g \ge 2p+2$ a depth-$p$ local algorithm sees the same tree around every edge, so its expected cut fraction on that tree bounds $M_g$ from below. We apply this strategy to the Variational Iterative Rotation Algorithm (VIRAL), a classical local algorithm, and evaluate it on the depth-$p$ tree for every even depth up to $p=32$. The resulting bounds exceed those recently obtained from the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) for every $p\ge 4$, by $0.005$ to $0.011$, and they extend the range of girths covered from $g=36$ to $g=66$. Notably, at $g=66$ we obtain $M_{66} \ge 0.9127$ at $99.99999\%$ confidence level, which raises the asymptotic lower bound from $0.912$ to $0.9127$.
item.dc:creator: Flaviano Morone, Shivang Rawat, Dries Sels

item.title: On the Statistical Mechanics of Attention
item.description: arXiv:2610.17347v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We revisit the statistical mechanics of Transformer attention via modern Hopfield models. We present a free-energy formalism to characterize parameter regimes and critical thresholds for robust attention inference. The resulting free-energy landscape incorporates randomness in query states and attention weights. Attention then emerges as the equation of motion of the corresponding statistical-mechanical system (i.e., modern Hopfield model) through the standard free-energy minimization principle. This allows us to identify first-order phase transitions in attention between glassy and robust-inference phases. We further extend to attentions with stochastic queries and keys. Together, our results provide a rigorous statistical-mechanics framework for characterizing phase structure and inference reliability across a family of Transformer attention mechanisms.
item.dc:creator: Jerry Yao-Chieh Hu, Yu-An Chen, Maojiang Su, Han Liu

item.title: Sampling from the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Model up to Criticality
item.description: arXiv:2610.17717v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the simulated annealing algorithm efficiently samples from the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at inverse temperature $\beta < 1$ to an arbitrary inverse polynomial accuracy in total variation.
item.dc:creator: Hang Du, Brice Huang, Sidhanth Mohanty, Amit Rajaraman

item.title: Supersymmetric Observables from Surface Defect Anomalies in 4d and 6d SCFTs
item.description: arXiv:2610.18086v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the contributions of half-BPS surface defects to supersymmetric Casimir energy and the universal logarithmic term of supersymmetric R\'enyi entropy in four- and six-dimensional SCFTs. Using equivariant integration of defect anomaly polynomials and its extension to supersymmetric R\'enyi backgrounds, we obtain closed expressions for these observables in terms of defect 't Hooft anomalies. For Gukov--Witten defects preserving transverse rotations in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = 4$ super Yang--Mills theories, both observables depend on a single R-symmetry anomaly. For $\mathcal{N} = (0, 4)$ defects in six-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = (1, 0)$ theories, additional terms arise from the gravitational anomaly. We provide complementary checks using chiral algebras, five-dimensional localization, and holographic probe branes at large $N$, while localized chiral fermions reproduce the gravitational-anomaly contributions. The framework also recovers Wilson-surface results in six-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = (2, 0)$ theories.
item.dc:creator: Zi-Xiao Huang, Ma-Ke Yuan, Yang Zhou

item.title: Free energy of non-convex multi-species Ising spin glasses with external fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.18350v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We identify the limit free energy of mean-field multi-species spin glasses with +/-1 spins, allowing for the presence of external fields, and without assuming any convexity property of the covariance function of the Hamiltonian. The limit is given by an "uninverted" variational formula over Brownian martingales. The proof consists in first identifying the limit free energy of configurations with a fixed magnetization. Once the magnetization is fixed, we can show the convergence of the enriched free energy to the solution of a Hamilton-Jacobi equation. The magnetization constraint is also used to show the convexity of the initial condition in this equation, and this yields a variational representation of the solution, as a Hopf formula. Convex duality then turns this formula into an optimization over martingales whose initial values are the prescribed magnetizations.
item.dc:creator: Jeanne Boursier, Jean-Christophe Mourrat

item.title: Altermagnetic Ground States on the Ammann--Beenker Tiling
item.description: arXiv:2610.18441v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We identify exact altermagnetic ground states of a classical Heisenberg model on a quasicrystal. Considering the Ammann--Beenker tiling as an example, we determine the ground states by exploiting the parity structure of its parent four-dimensional hypercubic lattice. The ground state hosts coplanar altermagnetic order characterized by the preserved spin-group symmetry $[C_{2x}\parallel C_{8z}]$. Without translational symmetry, the momentum-space spin splitting that usually identifies altermagnets is not directly accessible. We instead couple the spins to itinerant electrons and show spin-resolved transport with $g$-wave symmetry, confirming the altermagnetic nature in a nonperiodic system. Our results establish a geometric route to altermagnetic order in quasicrystals, connecting exact magnetic ground states to their spin-resolved transport signatures.
item.dc:creator: SeungBeom Hong, YunHo Kim, Moon Jip Park, GiBaik Sim

item.title: Extending the mean first-passage-time formalism to the reconstruction of high free-energy barriers: A top-start approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.18653v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rare events, such as crystal nucleation in mildly supercooled liquids, are characterized by waiting times that can be much longer than the timescale of the underlying microscopic dynamics. The mean first-passage time (MFPT) formalism [J. Wedekind and D. Reguera, J. Phys. Chem. B 112, 11060 (2008)] provides a route to reconstruct one-dimensional free-energy profiles from the MFPT and steady-state distribution measured along a reaction coordinate, but conventional implementations become inefficient for sufficiently high barriers because spontaneous crossings are rarely observed. We introduce a "top-start" extension that initiates trajectories near the barrier top and reconstructs the free-energy profile from their subsequent evolution away from the barrier toward lower-free-energy regions. We establish the equivalence between the top-start and two-region constructions using a Markov-chain transition-matrix formulation. We validate the method using one-dimensional random-walk simulations across low, medium, and high free-energy barriers, with transition-matrix calculations providing an exact benchmark for the corresponding discretized models. The top-start reconstruction remains accurate in the high-barrier regime where conventional MFPT sampling becomes prohibitively inefficient.
item.dc:creator: Ying Jiang, Ivan Saika-Voivod

item.title: Superexchange coupling between a dilute Gd3+ probe and orphan spins in a valence-bond glass
item.description: arXiv:2610.18722v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The valence-bond-glass state of the 4d^1 double perovskite Ba2YMoO6 combines Mo^5+ singlets with residual paramagnetic "orphan" spins whose coupling is hard to reach with bulk probes. We probe them by electron paramagnetic resonance of a dilute Gd^3+ ion on the Y^3+ site via broadband coplanar-waveguide transmission at 5 K. The isostructural nonmagnetic niobate Ba2YNbO6, doped with the same Gd^3+ probe, is a fixed-lattice control. The Gd^3+ linewidth nearly doubles in the magnetic host. Dipolar coupling to the sparse orphans is nearly an order of magnitude too weak; the excess is instead reproduced by a transferred f-d superexchange of J ~ 0.2 K, so the width is a static measure of orphan-spin coupling. The half-field (Delta m_S = +/-2) satellite collapses in the magnetic host, a dynamical dephasing channel, while the unchanged g-factor marks a zero-mean random internal field. Together the two channels probe the coupling and dynamics of valence-bond-glass orphan spins.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Colgan, Artur Solodovnyk, Jeremy P. Carlo, Scott Dietrich

item.title: The benefit of ignorance for traffic through a random congestible network
item.description: arXiv:2503.09684v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: When traffic is routed through a network that is susceptible to congestion, the self-interested decisions made by individual users do not, in general, produce the optimal flow. This discrepancy is quantified by the so-called ``price of anarchy.'' Here we consider whether the traffic produced by self-interested users is made better or worse when users have uncertain knowledge about the cost functions of the links in the network, and we define a parallel concept that we call the ``price of ignorance.'' We introduce a simple model in which fast, congestible links and slow, incongestible links are mixed randomly in a large network and users plan their routes with finite uncertainty about which of the two cost functions describes each link. One of our key findings is that a small level of user ignorance universally improves traffic, regardless of the network composition. Further, there is an optimal level of ignorance which, in our model, causes the self-interested user behavior to coincide with the optimum. Many features of our model can be understood analytically, including the optimal level of user ignorance and the existence of critical scaling near the percolation threshold for fast links, where the potential benefit of user ignorance is greatest. We demonstrate that our qualitative conclusions apply also to networks with nonlinear cost functions, and we comment on the case of scale-free networks, where there is no direct analog of percolation physics.
item.dc:creator: Alican Saray, Calvin Pozderac, Ari Josephson, Shravan Sripadhanallur Natarajan, Brian Skinner

item.title: Pseudo-critical localization
item.description: arXiv:2509.18943v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We uncover a novel localization phenomenon, termed pseudo-critical localization, in non-Hermitian critical systems. This phenomenon is induced by the synergistic interplay between weak localization and non-Hermitian skin effects. It exhibits critical-like behavior at finite scales and undergoes a crossover to Anderson localization as the system size increases, which is in sharp contrast to critical localization that universally exhibits persistent criticality in the thermodynamic limit. Concretely, we use the non-Hermitian quasiperiodic mosaic model and non-reciprocal Aubry--Andr\'e model as minimal models to present the general features of size-dependent critical localization, and use entanglement entropy analysis to confirm the size-dependent nature. This discovery challenges the established paradigm of critical localization, opening new avenues for understanding and controlling critical behavior in non-Hermitian systems.
item.dc:creator: Hui-Qiang Liang, Linhu Li, Guo-Fu Xu

item.title: Fock-space fragmentation in quenches of disordered interacting fermions
item.description: arXiv:2510.19510v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fock-space fragmentation, as it is currently investigated, primarily originates from specific kinematic constraints or emergent conservation laws in many-body systems with translation invariance. It leads to non-ergodic dynamics and possible breakdown of the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis. Here, we demonstrate that also in disordered systems, such as the XXZ model with random on-site fields, fragmentation appears as a natural concept offering fresh perspectives, for example, on many-body localization (MBL). Specifically, for a given quenched initial state, we identify a potential-energy shell in Fock space, defined by its energy and energy uncertainty, which represents the energetically accessible part of the many-body configuration space. For example, the drastic sample-to-sample fluctuations observed in the weak disorder regime, $W<W_{\mathrm{frag}}$, represent fluctuations of the mass of the shell. Upon increasing disorder, the potential-energy shell becomes increasingly fragmented. Its finite-size evolution exhibits a turnaround flow; extrapolating this flow to the disorder at which the turnaround vanishes provides a heuristic estimate of the strong-fragmentation scale $W_{\mathrm{frag}}$. We conjecture that the fragmentation identified here provides a geometric mechanism contributing to the finite-time slowing down of relaxation observed in studies of disordered interacting systems.
item.dc:creator: Ishita Modak, Rajesh Narayanan, Ferdinand Evers, Soumya Bera

item.title: Multifractality at the Integer Quantum Hall Transition: Acquittal of the Parabolic Law
item.description: arXiv:2606.21679v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Stationary wave functions at the integer quantum Hall transition are known to be multifractal, but the exact form of the multifractality spectrum has remained a subject of debate. While conformal field theory arguments predict a parabolic law, numerical simulations show deviations from parabolicity. We resolve this discrepancy by pointing out that powers of the local wave intensity fail to obey the Gaussian Free Field and Abelian Fusion Hypothesis assumed in earlier analysis. Rather, due to the non-Abelian nature of the underlying effective field theory, wave intensity correlators are dressed by insertions of background charge distributed uniformly in space. An exact expression for the $q$-moments of point-contact generated eigenstates is presented. Numerical tests are performed for the critical Chalker-Coddington network model on a rectangular torus. Our results are in precise agreement with the predictions of conformal symmetry realized as a level-4 current algebra.
item.dc:creator: Sen Mu, Abbas Ali Saberi, Martin R. Zirnbauer

item.title: Anderson localization on the Bethe lattice
item.description: arXiv:2606.24671v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Anderson localization - the suppression of wave propagation by interference in a sufficiently disordered medium - is one of the most remarkable phenomena in condensed matter physics. These lecture notes provide a pedagogical introduction to Anderson localization on the Bethe lattice, an infinite tree with fixed connectivity and no loops, and one of the few settings in which the transition can be studied exactly. The problem is important for two main reasons. First, the Anderson model on the Bethe lattice provides a mean-field, infinite-dimensional limit in which the transition point and critical behavior can be determined exactly. Second, it provides a simplified description of the high-dimensional configuration spaces of interacting quantum systems, and thus a useful toy model for many-body localization. We focus on the Green's function formalism and the cavity method. After recalling standard diagnostics of localization based on transport, spectral statistics, and eigenfunction moments, we show that they are encoded in the statistics of the Green's functions, and that the full distribution of the local density of states is the natural order parameter of the transition. We derive the exact self-consistent cavity equations on the Bethe lattice, use them to characterize the two phases and critical behavior - including an analytic solution at large connectivity - and describe population-dynamics algorithms that solve them with high precision. We explain how an exponentially large correlation volume and the localized nature of the critical point account for the strong finite-size effects on random regular graphs, which led to a long debate over a possible intermediate non-ergodic phase. Finally, we discuss the mapping onto directed polymers in random media, interpreting localization as a freezing transition dominated by a few rare resonant paths.
item.dc:creator: Dafne Prado Bandeira, Angelica Vecchiarelli, Marco Tarzia

item.title: Statistical Landscape Exploration and Weak-Field Defects in Selective Oscillator Ising Machines
item.description: arXiv:2609.14550v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Oscillator Ising machines (OIMs) provide an analog dynamical approach to combinatorial optimization, but comparatively little is known about the statistical structure of the ensembles they generate. Using the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (SK) spin-glass model, we introduce a selective oscillator scheme, OIM+, in which successive annealing epochs are combined with energy-based elimination and repopulation of replicas. We characterize the resulting states through overlap distributions, Hamming distances, hierarchical clustering, and local-field statistics. OIM+ explores structured low-energy regions while retaining a nontrivial ensemble of configurations despite repeated selection. We identify sparse weak-local-field residual defects as a characteristic limitation of the dynamics. A short Metropolis-Hastings refinement preferentially corrects these defects, indicating that the oscillator dynamics performs the dominant collective exploration while the remaining corrections are predominantly local. The weak fields arise mainly from cancellation among competing interaction terms rather than uniformly weak couplings. The same behavior persists for an antiferromagnetically biased SK ensemble, where the hybrid method reaches a pooled mean energy comparable to a substantially longer pure Metropolis anneal. The complete protocol also achieves competitive performance on standard G-set Max-Cut benchmarks. These results suggest a natural division of labor between collective analog search and targeted local refinement.
item.dc:creator: \"Omer \"Onder, Ayd{\i}n Cem Keser

item.title: Earthquake Dynamics as a Benchmark for Scale-Invariant Behavior
item.description: arXiv:2512.17615v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We analyze regional earthquake energy statistics from the Southern California and Japan seismic catalogs and find scale-invariant energy distributions characterized by an exponent $\tau \simeq 1.67$. To quantify how closely scale-invariant dynamics with different exponent values resemble real earthquakes, we generate synthetic energy distributions over a wide range of $\tau$ under conditions of constant activity. Earthquake-like behavior, in a broad sense, is obtained for $1.5 \leqslant \tau < 2.0$. When energy variations are further restricted to be within a factor of ten relative to real earthquakes, the admissible range narrows to $1.58 \leqslant \tau \leqslant 1.76$. We identify the physical mechanisms governing the dynamics in the different regimes: fault dynamics characterized by a balance between slow energy accumulation and release through scale-free events in the earthquake-like regime; externally supplied energy relative to a slowly driven fault for $\tau < 1.5$; and dominance of small events in the energy budget for $\tau > 2$
item.dc:creator: Kilian Duplat, German Varas, Osvanny Ramos

item.title: Limitations of Avila-inspired theory in the diamond chain with quasiperiodic disorder
item.description: arXiv:2603.12362v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The mobility edges (MEs) that separate localized, multifractal and ergodic states in energy are a central concept in understanding Anderson localization. In this work we study the effect of several mutually commensurate quasiperiodic frequencies on the mobility edge formation. We focus on the example of the addition of a constant offset to the quasiperiodic potential of the one-dimensional all-bands-flat diamond chain. We show that this additional offset can transform the anomalous mobility edges (AMEs), i.e. the energies, separating localized and multifractal states, into conventional mobility edges, separating localized from delocalized states. Also this appears to be the first example which shows the inability of Avila's global theory to analytically predict the ME location. We observe this both quantitatively, through the ME location mismatch, and qualitatively, via the formation of multiple MEs, not predicted by the theory.
item.dc:creator: Manish Kumar, Ivan M. Khaymovich, Auditya Sharma

item.title: Entanglement Growth from Structured Initial States in Many-Body Localized Systems
item.description: arXiv:2605.20656v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Understanding how complex entanglement structures emerge is a central problem in quantum many-body physics. Recent work by Zhang et al. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020404 (2026)] has considered structured initial states prepared by evolving a product state under a chaotic Hamiltonian for a finite time before quenching to the target Hamiltonian. In this setup, total entanglement entropy growth in many-body localized systems exhibits two distinct regimes, first increasing and then decreasing as the initial entanglement is tuned. In this work, we identify the physical origin of this behavior by analyzing the dynamics of both the R\'enyi entanglement entropy and the Wehrl-R\'enyi entropy in the random-field XXZ model, the latter of which characterizes multipartite entanglement. We show that a similar non-monotonic dependence on the initial entanglement also appears in the net growth of the Wehrl-R\'enyi entropy for product states polarized along the $z$-direction. The first regime is governed by a finite magnetization associated with local integrals of motion, while the second reflects inter-site correlations. In contrast, for product states in the $x/y$-direction, the entanglement growth exhibits a monotonic decay. Our results provide a more fine-grained picture of how distinct initial-state properties shape entanglement dynamics in many-body localized systems.
item.dc:creator: Chen Xu, Pengfei Zhang

item.title: Local network evolution rules driving shortest path multiplicity
item.description: arXiv:2605.25237v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The shortest path multiplicity, here denoted by $\mu$, is an important metric of complex networks. For real networks $\mu$ is high and it correlates with the network community structure. Since local network evolution induces network communities, it is possible that a high shortest path multiplicity is the natural expectation of local evolution rules. Here I demonstrate, by means of numerical simulations and exact results, that this is indeed the case. For random graphs with arbitrary degree distributions $p_k$, $\langle\mu\rangle\sim \langle k(k-1)\rangle / (\langle k\rangle e)$, growing with the network size when $p_k\sim k^{-\gamma}$ and $\gamma\leq3$. For networks generated by stochastic local rules, $\langle\mu\rangle$ increases with the network size and it does so faster than what is observed in their randomized versions. Furthermore, the number of communities increases with the network size and the correlation with $\langle \mu\rangle$ follows.
item.dc:creator: Alexei Vazquez

item.title: Two-dimensional Hyperbolic RNN Neural Quantum State
item.description: arXiv:2606.25600v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the first part of this work, we construct the first type of two-dimensional (2D) hyperbolic neural quantum state (NQS) in the form of the Lorentz 2DRNN (Recurrent Neural Network) and benchmark its performance against the Euclidean 2DRNN in the paradigmatic $N \times N$ 2D Transverse Field Ising Model (2DTFIM) setting with different lattice sizes up to N = 12 at different transverse magnetic field strengths. We find that hyperbolic Lorentz 2DRNN NQS robustly outperforms Euclidean 2DRNN NQS in our experiments when the system is at the phase transition point, where the physics can be described by a conformal field theory (CFT) - known via the AdS/CFT holographic duality to possess an underlying hyperbolic geometry. In the second part of this work, we benchmark the performances of recently introduced one-dimensional (1D) hyperbolic NQS ansatzes (including Poincare RNN/GRU and Lorentz RNN/GRU) against their Euclidean versions in $N \times N$ 2DTFIM, converted to a one-dimensional sequence. The findings extend our previous results showing that 1D hyperbolic NQS robustly outperforms 1D Euclidean NQS, thanks to the combined effects of the induced 1st and Nth neighbor interaction hierarchy and the CFT physics at criticality. While studies on larger system sizes remain future work, this study serves as a proof-of-concept for the utility, effectiveness, and superior performance of 1D and 2D hyperbolic NQS ansatzes compared to conventional Euclidean NQS models in many-body quantum systems - particularly those exhibiting structural hierarchy, criticality, or a combination of both.
item.dc:creator: H. L. Dao

item.title: The Information Content of Krylov Observables: A Machine Learning Approach
item.description: arXiv:2607.17346v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We employ machine learning techniques to estimate the amount of information contained in three Krylov-space observables: the spread complexity $C(t)$, the discrete Wigner negativity $N(t)$, and the normalized negativity $\chi(t)=N(t)/|S(t)|$, where $S(t)$ is the survival amplitude. We study thermofield-double evolutions on GUE, GOE and Poisson spectra, and on the integrable $SL(2,R)$ Krylov chain of a two-dimensional CFT primary, with Lanczos coefficients $b_n=\alpha\sqrt{n(n+2h-1)}$. To introduce chaos we add a GUE random matrix to the integrable chain, $H(\varepsilon)=H_{SL(2,R)}+\varepsilon R_0 W_{GUE}$, where $R_0$ is its spectral half-width. Either $C(t)$ or $N(t)$ alone determines the thermofield temperature, with $R^2\simeq0.999$. However, neither can reconstruct the fine structure of the spectral form factor. In the integrable sector all three observables carry the same information. When we turn on chaos an asymmetry appears: $\chi$ predicts $C$ better than $C$ predicts $\chi$. This gap grows from $+0.33$ to $+0.77$, while the same gap for the raw negativity decays to zero. The extra information comes from the survival amplitude, and $\chi(t)$ carries it while $C(t)$ can still be recovered from $\chi(t)$. We derive a lower bound on this gap, set by the fraction of the variance of $\chi$ that comes from $S$.
item.dc:creator: Ritam Basu
